summary: A lighthouse and fog signal on Tatoosh Island, the Makah summer island off the entrance to the Strait of Juan de Fuca, lit in 1857 and now closed and in disrepair.

access.note: Island owned by the Makah Tribe and closed except to permitted researchers; lighthouse visible from the Cape Flattery Trail on the mainland.

facts.agency: Makah Tribe (island); lighthouse transfer from the Coast Guard reported as pending in 2017

notes_for_editor: Pre-1891 construction and early-keeper detail rests on LighthouseFriends (secondary, which cites Light-House Board reports) because the local corpus holds no Board report before 1891; no newspaper pages were read (newspapers.py searches timed out), so the 1900, 1911 and 1934 drownings are LighthouseFriends only (it cites the SF Call, 9 Nov 1900). Sources disagree on automation (1976 National Trust, 1977 LighthouseFriends/Wikipedia), tower height (LF 66 ft; USLHS 64 ft; record 19.0 m; Wikipedia 65 ft), focal height (LF 162 ft; USLHS 155 ft; Wikipedia 165 ft), distance offshore (LF half mile; Trust three-quarters) and George K. Smith's end (archive 1864, LF transfer 1865). The 1913 Bulletin rescue date is February 10 of that volume (page not confirmed; PDF page about 14). Bulletin 1932 electrification text is badly OCR'd; quotes are fragments. LighthouseFriends's 1921 gale anecdote (70 mph, the keeper blown 300 feet, the bull) conflicts with the Bulletin's 110 mph reading and was left out. The 1932 lens swap is dated only 'recently' in the Bulletin. USLHS lists Leslie C. Valentine (1944) in LF but not in the archive roster. NRHP 72001267 is the nomination for Tatoosh Island itself (owner then Commander, 13th CG District); not used. Roster lines for later Coast Guard personnel are the archive's own 'USCG' list, role normalised to crew. 'Frank Reif' appears only in LighthouseFriends.
